title: Grove will only redeem Pendle principal tokens after market expiry, eliminating market-price risk from the operation
content:
A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.2.2.1.2.1.2.11 scopes the whole Pendle module to "redeem **expired** Pendle Principal Tokens (PT) for their underlying token", and A...11.1.2 enforces it: `require(params.pendleMarket.isExpired(), "PendleLib/market-not-expired")`.

The restriction is what makes the rest of the procedure simple. Before expiry a PT trades on an AMM at a discount that varies with time and implied yield, so selling it would require a price oracle, a tick or slippage bound, and all the machinery the Curve and Uniswap paths carry. After expiry a PT is redeemable at its accrued value, computed from `IYT(yt).pyIndexCurrent()` (A...11.1.3) — an index, not a market price.

So Grove deliberately declines the ability to exit a Pendle position early through this function. The trade-off is stark and worth naming: it removes execution-price risk entirely, at the cost of removing the early-exit option. Any pre-expiry exit must go through a general swap route instead, where the normal slippage controls apply.

The pattern generalises: narrowing a function's admissible state until the risky variable disappears is cheaper and more auditable than defending against the risky variable.
description: PendleLib reverts with market-not-expired unless pendleMarket.isExpired(); at expiry PT converts at the PY index, so redemption needs no AMM, oracle or price bound.
